metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth degradation waste GPU-hours before they cause outages, making continuous monitoring of the internal and external fabric essential for AI data centers.

Distributed AI training synchronizes gradients across thousands of GPUs in lockstep. A single percent of packet loss or a millisecond of added latency does not trigger an alarm in traditional infrastructure. In AI workloads it triggers compute stalls, where expensive hardware sits idle waiting for data that should have arrived. These stalls compound across the cluster. The facility must measure latency and loss continuously on both its internal network (connecting GPUs within the building) and external transit (connecting to other facilities or users) to catch degradation before it translates into wasted training time.

This metric captures a class of failures distinct from total outages. A data center can pass an SLA uptime check while its network fabric silently converts weeks of compute into nothing. The measure matters specifically because AI workloads are unusually intolerant of the network problems that other workloads tolerate or work around. It does not measure compute density, power delivery, or cooling. It measures only whether the path between compute and compute is open.
